## Zone 1 — Rulings (not re-litigable)

Two maintainer rulings govern this card.

1. **2026-08-20, verbatim C** superseded the `$schema` half of the 2026-08-19 ruling. PR #5334 deleted `OBJECTUI_SCHEMA_URL` and `pointsAtObjectUi()` before merge. There is deliberately **no `$schema` arm** and no ObjectUI `$schema` URL exists to declare.
2. **2026-08-25 on #5392 — Option B, no shipped artifact.** Maintainer accepted the batch recommendation verbatim: 「同意你的建议」. That discharged this card's blocker, and the routing comment of 10:13Z records the ruled route:

> the ruled route for this card is **`safeValidateSchema` as the recogniser** — measured under #5392 / PR #6203: over the 309 skipped files it admits 209 and refuses all 45 `package.json`, strictly better than the schema artifact would have been (223 admitted / 14 false-accepts). The `$schema`-arm route stays foreclosed while #5392 holds (no artifact exists to point at).

⛔ Therefore: **do not** add a `$schema` arm, **do not** mint a URL, **do not** stamp markers into the corpus (that prohibition is what #5329 died on), and **do not** widen `OBJECTUI_STRUCTURAL_KEYS` — #5334 measured `label` as held out *by name* because admitting `BaseSchema`-adjacent naming keys drives foreign retention from 0 files toward all 46. A key that recovers leaf schemas but starts judging `package.json` is a net loss.

## The design question this card owns — answer it explicitly

Carried from the routing comment, and it is the part that needs your judgement rather than transcription:

> a validity-based recogniser conflates "foreign file" with "broken ObjectUI schema" — files failing validation today would be filed as not-ObjectUI rather than reported as invalid. The implementation must decide how that bucket is reported; **silently reclassifying invalid ObjectUI content as foreign is the failure mode to avoid.**

⭐ This is the load-bearing part of the change. A recogniser that says "not ObjectUI" about a genuinely broken ObjectUI file makes the checker quietly *less* able to find the thing it exists to find, and the symptom is an absence — the file simply stops being mentioned. Decide how that bucket surfaces, implement it, and state the decision and its cost in your PR body. Measure the bucket's size rather than assuming it is empty.

## Zone 2 — PM mechanism readings (verify; some will have moved)

Read on `origin/main` @ `090927f4f` at 11:55Z:

- `safeValidateSchema` is exported from `@object-ui/types/zod` and already consumed by `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:13` and `:58`. So `objectui check` and `objectui validate` would share one recogniser — worth saying in the PR whether that coupling is intended, because it makes `check`'s recall move whenever validation tightens.
- `OBJECTUI_STRUCTURAL_KEYS` lives at `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts:35`, is used at `:128`, and is printed to the user at `:255`. If your change alters what gets judged, that user-facing sentence at `:255` is part of the change — an explanation that no longer describes the predicate is the same defect class as the comment #6074 just fixed.
- ⚠️ **Every count on this card is a snapshot and they all move.** 617 globbed / 475 eligible / 166 judged / 309 skipped / 263 real / 46 foreign, and the earlier stamped table said 304/258 five days before it said 309/263 — the surface **grew**. ⛔ Re-measure and cite your own numbers; do not adopt any figure from this card, from #5329, or from this order.
- The 209/45 measurement in the ruling came from #5392 / PR #6203. Re-derive it against your base rather than quoting it — if `safeValidateSchema` admits materially fewer than the ruling expects, that is a finding worth stopping on, not a number to quietly ship past.

## Zone 3 — Suggested route (optional; measurement wins)

Replace the marker predicate's negative arm with a validity probe, keep the structural-key arm as the fast path, and give the skip report three buckets instead of two: judged, foreign (refused by the recogniser and structurally implausible), and *candidate ObjectUI content that failed validation* — the last one reported rather than swallowed. ⛔ My guess at the shape, not a constraint; if the honest design is two buckets plus a diagnostic, take that and say why.

Keep the printed count honest either way. The card is explicit: the debt's visibility in the printed count is the point — ⛔ do not silence it, and do not let the number fall because files moved into an unreported bucket.

## Gates

Derive from your diff. A recall change needs a test that pins the new behaviour on real corpus shapes — including at least one genuinely invalid ObjectUI file, so the bucket decision above is pinned and not just described. `packages/cli` is a released package, so follow `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s verdict. Capture exit codes by redirect **before** any pipe; quote each gate's own verdict line, not its exit code.

⛔ Do not edit `content/docs/releases/`.

## Standing

Worktree-first before your first edit. Post **your own claim comment** here with your own session ID and branch — this one identifies the PM session, not you. Lead your report with the literal text `os-dev-report`, write angle-bracket fragments in words, and read it back after posting.

Expected outcome: `done` with a draft PR carrying `Fixes #6075`. `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is a legitimate delivery if the debt has already been repaid by something merged since 10:13Z.

## ACCEPT — PR #6322

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R30. Read against the diff on GitHub, ⛔ not against the report's summary.

### Checklist

| Criterion | Reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR form | draft ✅, base `main` ✅ |
| Diff | 5 files: `check.ts` (+135/−32), a new 280-line test file, the existing marker suite, `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx`, a changeset |
| Ruled route | `safeValidateSchema` as the second arm, structural arm first ✅ |
| Prohibitions | `OBJECTUI_STRUCTURAL_KEYS` unchanged ✅ · no `$schema` arm ✅ · no URL minted ✅ · no corpus marker stamped ✅ · `packages/types` untouched, no export widened ✅ |
| Governed surface | clean. Normal landing path. |
| Changeset | present (`@object-ui/cli` minor), and the gate's verdict was that one **is** owed here — matching, unlike the other two PRs this round |
| CI | `Bundle Analysis` ✅ among 27 checks; zero failures, several still running at review time |

### The design question this card owns — answered, and the answer is measured

The card required a decision on the failed-validation bucket, and warned that silently reclassifying broken ObjectUI content as foreign is the failure to avoid. The answer shipped is **three buckets**, and the accounting closes on my own arithmetic: **375 judged (166 structural + 209 validity) + 54 reported + 46 skipped = 475 eligible**, against 166/309 before.

⭐ **The bucket was measured rather than assumed to be small: 54 files, 53 of them real corpus content.** A two-bucket recogniser would have filed 53 genuinely broken schemas as "not ObjectUI" — so the hazard the card named was not hypothetical, it was 53 files wide.

The discriminator is `isKnownSchemaType` — the same derived registered-type universe the judgement arm already uses, so it adds no second hand-maintained list. That is the right choice: a filename skip list is what #5127 existed to delete.

**Its cost is declared and pinned rather than hidden**: a foreign document whose root `type` collides with a registered component key (a draft-07 JSON Schema with `"type": "object"`) lands in the report as one advisory line. There is a test asserting exactly that, with a comment explaining why the opposite error is the worse one. A cost with a test on it is a known cost.

### The tests are where this PR earns its acceptance

Half the new suite is **negative** — written to fail if a future simplification collapses the third bucket back into two. The one I would single out:

> `it('mentions it by name even when it is the only file in the project')`

That is an **absence-detector**: it fails when the command goes quiet, which is the only symptom this defect class has. A suite that merely proved the newly-recognised files are judged would have passed the very regression the card was filed about. The ablation confirms it bites — collapsing `isUnvalidatedCandidate` to `false` reds 8 tests, with the mutation proven on disk by blob hash before any result was read.

The honest-limit test is the other one worth naming: an unregistered root `type`, no structural key, and a document that does not validate is byte-for-byte the evidence a foreign file offers, so it stays in the skip count. Pinning that as a deliberate limit rather than leaving it as an unexplained residue is the right instinct.

### Two things I checked because they would have been easy to get wrong

- **The printed count stays honest.** The card was explicit that the debt's visibility is the point. 309 → 46 is not a number that fell because files moved into an unreported bucket — 209 became judged and 54 are listed **by name and uncapped**, printed *before* the skip count.
- **The user-facing explanation now describes the predicate it runs.** `check.ts:255`'s sentence named one arm; it now names both, with a test asserting two advisory lines and asserting the absence of any `$schema` or `http` string. That closes the same defect class #6074 had just removed from this file — an explanation that stopped describing the code.

⚠️ **One coupling to carry forward, correctly flagged in the diff's own docblock**: `check`'s recall is now tied to `@object-ui/types`' Zod schemas, so tightening a schema moves files out of recognition. That is survivable precisely *because* of the third bucket — a file that stops validating stops being judged but does not stop being mentioned. Worth remembering the next time someone tightens a schema and the numbers move.

Clause-② stays `no`: this changes which files `check` judges, not what the contract accepts or rejects, and `packages/types` is untouched.

### Out-of-scope findings — verified, and labelled

**#6318** (53 files carrying a registered type that fail validation, with the Zod-4 `invalid_union` collapse noted) and **#6320** (`objectui check` scans build output — the `dist/**` ignore is matched relative to cwd, so only a top-level `dist/` is excluded: **617 files on a clean checkout vs 1047 after a full build**) both exist and are well-formed. Both were filed **unlabelled**; I added `finding` to each.

⚠️ Correcting myself from earlier this round: I wrote on #6245 that an unlabelled card "could never have been seen" by triage. That overstates it — triage's sweep also picks up fully-naked cards, so these were reachable. The `finding` label is still what the protocol asks a dev to apply, and it marks the card as awaiting first grading, which is why I added it. But "invisible" was wrong.

⭐ #6320 also explains why every count in this report is qualified "clean checkout", and it means **the numbers on this card are checkout-state dependent** — worth knowing before anyone re-measures and gets roughly double.

### Landing

Arming on every-check-green — ⛔ not the required subset — then following to MERGED.
